Summary Description: Dr. Sanjana Mudduluru's research focuses on advancing medical image analysis through data-centric, multi-task deep learning approaches and data augmentation strategies that are practical for limited data regimes. Her work includes the development of J-Net, a joint segmentation-classification model for skin lesion analysis that leverages a shared encoder to improve both segmentation and classification, particularly in small datasets. She explores two-stage transfer learning to curate artifact-free retinal fundus datasets and improve classification reliability, using thresholding to separate easy and difficult cases and retraining on the difficult subset. She also proposes a lightweight, non-GAN synthetic data generation pipeline to dramatically expand medical image training data by projecting real lesion blobs onto healthy backgrounds in retinal imaging, yielding consistent performance gains across architectures. Her contributions span dermatology and ophthalmology imaging, with a strong emphasis on data quality, reproducibility, and practical deployment in clinical AI pipelines.
